newsitem.title: EGYPT: Egypt offers at least 10 pct of cotton ginner.
newsitem.headline: Egypt offers at least 10 pct of cotton ginner.

text.p: The Egyptian state said on Monday it was offering investors at least 10 percent or 292,160 shares in Wadi Cotton Ginning at an initial price of 44.5 pounds ($13.1) per share.
The state-owned Textile Manufacturing and Trade holding company firm said in an announcement that investors can bid for a minimum of 1,000 shares in its subsidary.
The state will sell an additional 10 percent of the firm to its employees.
The share offer will open for two days from July 14. State-owned Banque Misr is one of the agents for the sale which is part of the Egyptian government's privatisation-led economic reform programme.
The announcement said that Wadi Cotton Ginning's net profits for the third quarter of the current 1996/7 financial year were 13.68 million pounds. It did not give comparative figures.
The firm forecast net profits for the whole of 1996/7, which ended on June 30, would be 7.28 million pounds, recovering from a 1.99 million pound loss for 1995/6.

Net sales for the third quarter which ended on March 31, 1997 were 137.42 million pounds, with no significant changes forecast for the end of the year. Net sales were up from the 17.163 million of the 1995/6 financial year.
